evidenceAudit.scope: Acute and chronic hyperkalaemia in adults in India: severity, electrocardiogram (ECG) assessment, cardiac protection with calcium, shifting potassium into cells, removing potassium, dialysis, monitoring and safe use of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, built on the ICMR Acute Kidney Injury STW (July 2026) and the UK Kidney Association (UKKA) guideline (updated July 2026).
findings: Calcium gluconate 10 mL of 10% over 2–5 minutes under ECG monitoring repeatable up to 3 times, salbutamol 10 mg nebulised, insulin 10 units in 50 mL of 50% or 100 mL of 25% dextrose, withholding ACE inhibitors and ARBs, binders if dialysis is unavailable and urgent dialysis if life-threatening checked against the ICMR AKI STW (July 2026).

Severity bands, ECG and monitoring rules, the UKKA calcium dose (6.8 mmol: 30 mL of 10% calcium gluconate or 10 mL of 10% calcium chloride), insulin with 25 g glucose, post-treatment 10% glucose if pre-treatment glucose below 7.0 mmol/L, salbutamol 10–20 mg, sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) 10 g three times daily for up to 72 hours, patiromer 8.4 g, potassium and glucose monitoring schedules and RAAS inhibitor rules checked against UKKA (July 2026).
Calcium polystyrene sulfonate doses from the Calcium Resonium SmPC.
unverifiedSections: ICMR and UKKA give different calcium gluconate volumes (10 mL vs 30 mL of 10%) and dextrose regimens; both are shown, not merged.
UKKA no longer recommends calcium polystyrene sulfonate routinely for acute hyperkalaemia; it is listed because SZC and patiromer may be unavailable in Indian hospitals.
The sodium bicarbonate dose was not in the opened UKKA extract.
Paediatric hyperkalaemia is outside the scope of the cited adult guidelines, except the calcium polystyrene sulfonate paediatric dose from its SmPC.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Hyperkalaemia is serum potassium of 5.5 mmol/L or more; 6.5 mmol/L or more is severe (UKKA). It lowers the resting membrane potential of cardiac cells, slowing conduction and risking bradycardia, ventricular fibrillation or asystole. Common causes in India are acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease, RAAS inhibitors, potassium-sparing diuretics, diabetic ketoacidosis and tissue breakdown. Treatment follows a fixed order: protect the heart with IV calcium if the ECG shows changes, shift potassium into cells with insulin-glucose and salbutamol, remove potassium with binders or dialysis, and monitor potassium and glucose closely (UKKA; ICMR STW).
keyMechanisms: Raised extracellular potassium partly depolarises myocytes, inactivating sodium channels and slowing conduction.
Calcium restores the threshold potential without lowering potassium.
Insulin and beta-2 agonists drive potassium into cells via Na+/K+-ATPase.
Binders and dialysis are the only treatments that remove potassium from the body.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Repeat potassium if haemolysis likely, but treat at once if ECG changes (UKKA).
12-lead ECG for potassium 6.0 or more; cardiac monitor for 6.5 or more or ECG changes (UKKA 14.1–14.2).
Stop potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and mineralocorticoid antagonists (ICMR STW; UKKA 2.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Protect the heart
actions: IV calcium under ECG monitoring (see medicines); repeat if ECG changes persist (ICMR STW).
Calcium chloride in cardiac arrest or peri-arrest; gluconate otherwise (UKKA 16.2b).

clinicalManagement.title: Shift potassium into cells
actions: Insulin with glucose for severe hyperkalaemia; suggested for moderate (UKKA 16.3).
Add nebulised salbutamol in severe hyperkalaemia; never as sole treatment (UKKA 16.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Remove potassium
actions: Potassium binder: SZC for severe and consider for moderate (UKKA 16.6); binders if dialysis unavailable (ICMR STW).
Urgent dialysis if life-threatening or resistant (ICMR STW; UKKA 19.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor
actions: Potassium at 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 hours for moderate or severe (UKKA 17.1.2).
Glucose at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300 and 360 minutes after insulin (UKKA 17.2).
Restart RAAS inhibitors one at a time when potassium below 5.5 mmol/L (UKKA).
